guarantees.claim: all_written is 1 when every bit of we_d is 1.
none_written is 1 when no bit of we_d is 1.
new_d is 0 when clear_i or use_i is 1, otherwise equals all_written.
clean_d is 0 if clear_i is 1; else 1 if all_written is 1; else clean_q if none_written is 1; else 0.

assumptions.claim: Each set bit in we_d corresponds to a completed write of fresh data to a specific register; the external logic must ensure that a we_d bit is set only when the corresponding data register has been updated with a valid new value.
assumptions.cond: Whenever we_d is evaluated by this chunk.
assumptions.risk: Stale or garbage data may be incorrectly marked as all_written, causing the system to proceed with insecure (old/zeroized) key material.

uncertain_points.claim: clean_d is unaffected by use_i; if the architecture requires zeroization after every use, external logic must assert clear_i to invalidate the clean status.
uncertain_points.cond: use_i asserted while clear_i is not.
uncertain_points.risk: Key material may remain marked clean and potentially readable after use, violating required wipe/zeroization.

uncertain_points.claim: It is unclear whether we_d bits are cleared when clear_i is asserted. If they are not cleared, all_written may remain high, causing new_d to reassert to 1 immediately after clear_i deasserts, even though register contents may have been wiped.
uncertain_points.cond: clear_i deasserted while we_d retains previous write assertions.
uncertain_points.risk: new_d may falsely indicate a valid new value, allowing the system to consume cleared/zeroized data.
